candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; related activity statement: ‘Advocate for client rights and needs’
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — client rights and access to health information
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that HIPAA generally gives individuals access to PHI in designated record sets and, when PHI is maintained electronically, a right to an electronic copy in a readily producible requested format, subject to limited denial grounds.

options.A: The hospital may provide only a paper copy whenever paper is easier for staff to produce.
options.B: The client generally may receive an electronic copy in a requested readily producible format, subject to limited grounds for denial.
options.C: The client must explain why the records are needed before an electronic copy can be released.
options.D: Electronic access is optional under HIPAA and depends entirely on the hospital’s internal policy.

candidate.rationale: B is correct. Under 45 CFR §164.524, individuals generally have a right to access PHI about themselves in a designated record set. When the PHI is maintained electronically, the individual generally has a right to an electronic copy; if the requested electronic form and format are readily producible, the covered entity must provide that form and format, and otherwise must provide a readable alternative electronic format agreed to by the individual and covered entity, subject to the limited grounds for denial in §164.524(a). A is incorrect because a covered entity generally cannot substitute paper merely because it is easier when an electronic copy is required and a readily producible electronic format is available. C is incorrect because an individual is not required to state a purpose for exercising the right of access. D is incorrect because the access right arises from HIPAA and is not left entirely to facility discretion.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Individuals generally have a right to access PHI in designated record sets; if PHI is maintained electronically, they generally have a right to an electronic copy in the requested readily producible form and format, or an agreed readable alternative electronic format, subject to limited denial grounds.
candidate.source_document_title: Individuals’ Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information — 45 CFR §164.524
candidate.source_locator: 45 CFR §164.524(a), (c)(2)(ii); HHS guidance headings ‘General Right’ and ‘Under the HIPAA Privacy Rule, do individuals have the right to an electronic copy of their PHI?’
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
candidate.stem: A client asks a HIPAA-covered hospital for an electronic copy of protected health information (PHI) in a designated record set that the hospital maintains electronically. Which response by the nurse best reflects the client’s HIPAA right of access?
